rounds.text: Swastika Investmart Ltd carries fundamental risks and severe cash flow pressures that undermine its headline metrics. Compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has turned negative at -10% [E17], and compounded profit growth over the same period stands at -21% [E21], accompanied by flagged poor long-term sales growth of 8.88% over the past five years [E59]. Most critically, the business is burning cash, evidenced by a deeply negative operating cash flow of Rs -21 Cr [E35] and free cash flow of Rs -22 Cr [E36] in March 2026, leading to a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -1.40x [E34]. This deterioration is compounded by rising borrowings of Rs 9 Cr up from zero a year earlier [E39], alongside concerning contingent liabilities of Rs 84.5 Cr [E60] and a high perceived cost of borrowing [E61]. Furthermore, insiders are reducing their stake, with promoter holdings declining by 3.54 percentage points over the last three years down to 59.88% [E41, E62]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.07x [E38] and an operating margin expansion to 28% in the TTM [E30].
